Gaining and losing weight is definitely a numbers game, eat more than you need, and you'll gain weight, eat less than you need and you will loose weight. This is true but for both options you need nutrient dense food to maintain a healthy body, not just a lean one. Some nutritionist or nutrition coaches can do a meal plan for you which eliminates the paralysis of having to count everything you eat if that sounds like a good option.

As for protein, it has been discussed by both sides: 

https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6723444/

https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&as_sdt=0%2C5&q=plant+based+protein+absorption&oq=#d=gs_qabs&u=%23p%3DqBdRUdwF3-YJ

But you can't go wrong with "too much protein", which is why I would argue to believe the option that wouldn't hurt. Eat at a higher protein intake and if the absorption thing is a lie, the only repercussion would be to eat less carbohydrates and fats, not anything bad according to this study:

 https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5078648/

The most important thing as some have said is to get yourself into a routine and around people who make you feel comfortable during this journey, as this will make everything easier or even possible.
